full_judgment:
2. Material facts of the case, briefly, are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit being Title Suit No 300 of 2012 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for declaration that Memo No. বিপিসি.....প্রশাসন ৩৪.১৯ (অংশ)/০৬.২৬(ট)/৯৭ dated 1-3-2012 issued under the signature of defendant-opposite party No.3 is illegal, inoperative and without jurisdiction along with further declaration that Memo No. o8.৩৪.১৯/বিপনন/৪৯৭ dated 21-11-2010 issued under the signature of defendant-opposite party No.4 is also illegal, inoperative and without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff-petitioner. The plaintiff's case, in-short, is that the company represented by him is a reputed private limited company established under the Company Act, 1913 and the defendant-Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation established under Petroleum Corporation Ordinance, 1976 an autonomous body under the Government engaged in producing various petroleum products and marketing. According to sections 4(1) and (2) of the Petroleum Act, 1974 no person shall carry on any petroleum operation except under a petroleum agreement with the corporation. The plaintiff-petitioner has entered into a petroleum agreement with the defendants on 25-4-2011 and since then started marketing with the products of the corporation with full satisfaction. The defendant No.3 after being influenced by the vested quarters published an office circular under Memo No. বিপিসি/প্রশাসন/০৬২৬(ট)/৪০৫ তারিখ ২৪-১০-২০১১ stating “ব্যবহিত ট্রান্সফরমাল অয়েল রিফিইনিং এর জন্য সুনিদিষ্ট কোন নীতিমালা না থাকায় পরবর্তী নির্দেশ না দেওয়া পর্যন্ত ইতিপূর্বে ব্যবহৃত ট্রান্সফরমার অয়েল রিসাইকিং পূর্বক বাজারজাত করার ক্ষেত্রে বিপিসির সাথে চুক্তির হওয়ায় আবশ্যকতা আরোপের সংক্রান্ত বিপিসির পত্র সূ্ত্র বিপিসি/প্রশাসন/০৬২৬(ট)/৪০৫ তারিখ ২৪-১০-২০১৩ মূলে জারীকৃত নির্দেশনা এতদ্বারা বাতিল করা হল । The defendant opposite party No.2 issued the disputed circular by violating the clear provision of sections 4(1) and (2) of the Bangladesh Petroleum Act, 1974 with intent to give undue and illegal benefit to defendant No.5 and, as such, the impugned circular dated 24-10-2011 and 21-11-2010 are liable to be declared illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff. In view of the fact that since the defendant opposite party Nos. 1-4 have allowed the defendant No. 5 to marketing with petroleum products without written agreement and deposit of service charge by violating the mandatory provision of section 4(1) & (2) of the Bangladesh Petroleum Act, 1974 causing irreparable financial loss and injury to the plaintiff and hence, the suit. 

 3. Immediately after institution of the suit the plaintiff filed an application under Order XXXIX, Rule i and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for temporary injunction restraining the defendant No.1, Petroleum Corporation from allowing any person to deal with the petroleum products except under a petroleum agreement according to provision of section 4(1) and (2) of the Bangladesh Petroleum Act, 1974 and also restraining the defendant corporation from executing the office order under Memo No. বিপিসি.....প্রশাসন ৩৪.১৯ (অংশ)/০৬.২৬(ট)/৯৭ dated 1-3-2012 issued by the defendant No.3 and office circular under Memo No. বিপিসি.....প্রশাস�� ৩৪.১৯ (অংশ)/০৬.২৬(ট)/৯৭ issued under the signature of the defendant No.4 as well as restraining the defendant No.5 from marketing petroleum products of defendant No.1 in violating the provision of sections 4(1) and (2) of the Bangladesh Petroleum Act, 1974. 

 4. The defendant No.1 resisted the application for temporary injunction by filing written objection on the grounds that: (i) the plaintiff-petitioner has no locus standi to file the suit and make prayer for injunction, (ii) the defendant-opposite party is an autonomous body and has the right to formulate its own administrative measures, (iii) the defendants have not violated the terms of the agreement and (iv) the defendant No.1 is an autonomous corporation and has the legal right to issue administrative orders. 

 5. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka upon hearing the parties by his order dated 3-7-2012 rejected the application for temporary injunction on the finding that the plaintiff has no locus standi to make prayer for an order of injunction restraining the Petroleum Corporation from allowing any person to deal with the petroleum products except under a petroleum agreement as per provisions of sections 4(1) and (2) of the Bangladesh Petroleum Act, 1974. 

 6. The unsuccessful plaintiff, thereupon, preferred Misc. Appeal No.214 of 2012 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka, which was eventually transferred to the Court of Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka for disposal, who by the impugned judgment and order dated 26-2-2013 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the order passed by the trial Court below on the finding that balance of convenience and inconvenience is not in favour of the plaintiff rather it is in favour of the defendant, petroleum corporation. 

 8. Mr. Yousuf Hossain Humayun, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioner in the course of his argument after placing the impugned judgment as well as the order of the trial Court below along with other connected documents submits that both the Courts below misconceived the facts of the case and law bearing on the subject and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. He next submits that admittedly the petitioner executed an agreement with the Petroleum Corporation for 2(two) years on 25-4-2011 and thereafter it was renewed time to time for dealing business with regard to petroleum products and, as such, he has legal right to protect his business interest though both the courts below failed to consider that section 4(1) and (2) of the Bangladesh Petroleum Act, 1974 provided that "(i) the Government may enter into a petroleum agreement with any person for the purpose of any petroleum operation and (ii) no person shall undertake or carry on any petroleum operation except under a petroleum agreement entered into under sub-section (i)" and in this case the defendant opposite party No.2 issued the disputed circular by violating the clear provision of section 4(1) and (2) of the Bangladesh Petroleum Act, 1974 with intent to give undue and illegal benefit to defendant No.5 which occasioned a failure of justice. 

 10. Mr Md Abdul Hai, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, on the other hand, appearing for the opposite party Nos.1-4 supports the impugned judgment as well as order of the trial Court below. The learned Deputy Attorney-General in the course of his argument after placing the relevant law with regard to Petroleum Corporation submits that the present suit filed by the plaintiff-petitioner challenging the circular dated 1-3-2012 and 21-11-2010 is plainly misconceived inasmuch as in view of the express provision of section 27 of the Bangladesh, Petroleum Corporation Ordinance, 1976 and section 10 of the Petroleum Law, no suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings lie against the Chairman, any Director or any officer, adviser, consultant or employee of the Corporation for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this Ordinance. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that it is now well settled that in order to get an order of injunction the petitioner has to show that he has a strong prima facie case but in the instant case the plaintiff-petitioner has miserably failed to make out a prima facie case in his favour and taking the same into consideration the Courts below rightly rejected the prayer for injunction. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that the Courts of facts below were perfectly justified in refusing the petitioner's prayer for temporary injunction on the clear finding that plaintiff has no prima facie case for injunction as in the facts and circumstance of the case balance of convenience and inconvenience is in favour of the defendant-opposite party No. 1. 

 12. I have heard the learned Advocates and the learned Deputy Attorney-General at length and perused the revisional application, impugned judgment and other materials on record including the connected law and Ordinance. The facts of the case have already been set out so, I need not to repeat the same again. Now, to appreciate the points raised by the learned Advocates, I feel it necessary to decide first whether the Courts below were justified in refusing the petitioner's prayer for temporary injunction on the finding that plaintiff has no prima facie arguable case for injunction inasmuch as in the facts and circumstances of the case balance of convenience and inconvenience is in favour of the defendant-opposite party No. 1. 

 16. I have already noticed that the plaintiff-petitioner filed Title Suit No. 300 of 2012 challenging the circular and order dated 1-3-2012 and 21-11-2010 issued by the defendant-petroleum corporations which are required to be referred to for determining the real question of controversy.  19. Taking everything into consideration, I think that both the Courts of facts below were perfectly justified in refusing the petitioner's prayer for temporary injunction on the clear finding that the petitioner has failed to make out a prima-facie arguable case for getting an order of injunction retraining the defendant No.1, Petroleum Corporation from allowing any person to deal with the petroleum products except under a petroleum agreement. In any event, this is not a case in which the Court has jurisdiction to grant the relief asked for by the plaintiff-petitioner. 

 20. Having regard to the facts of the case and the reasons given by the Courts below, I do not think the refusal of injunction was either illegal, improper or inequitable. To avoid any prejudice to the plaintiff in the suit, it is better to refrain from making any further observation.
